SPQR V1: polynomial erasure coding (src/encoding/polynomial.rs, src/encoding.rs)

Trusted in part. The theorems of Computational/Theorems/ use only part of this file (see Computational/docs/TRUSTED_BASE.md): the rest (the OptionEncoder / OptionDecoder functions, the run*Guard self-tests, isOkEq / isErrEq / isOkErrEq, PolyConst.wf and Pt.eq) is checked by Lean.

Models SPQR's 32-byte chunk erasure code (Chunk) over $\mathrm{GF}(2^{16})$ with explicit panic (PolyPanic) and error (PolynomialError, EncodingError) values:

  • Pt (cmp, eq comparing x only) and SortedSetPt (len, replace, push, where pushing an existing x overwrites the stored Pt);

  • Poly (zero, lagrangeInterpolate, fromCompletePoints, computeAt) and fixed-length PolyConst (PolyConst.wf) for precomputed complete-point Lagrange bases;

  • PolyEncoder (encodeBytes, chunkAt, nextChunk, intoPb, fromPb via ProtoPolynomialEncoder) and PolyDecoder (new, addChunk, decodedMessage, intoPb, fromPb via ProtoPolynomialDecoder);

  • kernel-checked guard theorems (pt_serialize_and_ord_guard, …, option_encoder_decoder_guard).

def replaceL180–189 ↗#

SortedSet::replace (sorted-vec-0.8.11/src/lib.rs:386–402): overwrites an existing point with matching x and returns some old, or inserts in x-order and returns none.

def replace (self : SortedSetPt) (element : Pt) : SortedSetPt × Nat × Option Pt := match self.binarySearch element with | .ok existingIndex => let old := self.vec[existingIndex]? ({ vec := self.vec.set existingIndex element }, existingIndex, old) | .error insertIndex => let vec' := self.vec.take insertIndex ++ (element :: self.vec.drop insertIndex) ({ vec := vec' }, insertIndex, none)

def pushL191–207 ↗#

SortedSet::push (sorted-vec-0.8.11/src/lib.rs:413–438): appends at the back when element.x > last.x, replaces last when element.x == last.x, and delegates to replace when element.x < last.x.

def push (self : SortedSetPt) (element : Pt) : SortedSetPt × Nat × Option Pt := match self.vec.getLast? with | some last => match Pt.cmp element last with | .gt => let newVec := self.vec ++ [element] ({ vec := newVec }, newVec.length - 1, none) | .eq => let newVec := self.vec.dropLast ++ [element] ({ vec := newVec }, newVec.length - 1, some last) | .lt => self.replace element | none => ({ vec := [element] }, 0, none)
end SortedSetPt

def multXdiffAssignTrailingLoopL224–235 ↗#

def multXdiffAssignTrailingLoop (difference : GF16) : Nat → Nat → List GF16 → Except PolyPanic (List GF16) | _, 0, coeffs => .ok coeffs | i, rem + 1, coeffs => if i == 0 then .error .subOverflow else match coeffs[i]?, coeffs[i - 1]? with | some ci, some ciPrev => let delta := GF16.mul ci difference let coeffs' := coeffs.set (i - 1) (GF16.sub ciPrev delta) multXdiffAssignTrailingLoop difference (i + 1) rem coeffs' | _, _ => .error .boundsCheck

def multXdiffAssignTrailingL237–246 ↗#

Poly::mult_xdiff_assign_trailing (src/encoding/polynomial.rs:179–186): multiplies self[start..] by $(x - \mathrm{difference})$, propagating carry into self[start - 1] (.subOverflow if start == 0 and self.coefficients is non-empty).

def multXdiffAssignTrailing (self : Poly) (start : Nat) (difference : GF16) : Except PolyPanic Poly := do let l := self.coefficients.length if start >= l then return self else let coeffs' ← multXdiffAssignTrailingLoop difference start (l - start) self.coefficients return { coefficients := coeffs' }

def lagrangeInterpolatePrepareLoopL248–256 ↗#

def lagrangeInterpolatePrepareLoop (pts : List Pt) (offset : Nat) : Nat → Nat → Poly → Except PolyPanic Poly | _, 0, p => .ok p | i, rem + 1, p => do let some pi := pts[i]? | .error .boundsCheck if i > offset then .error .subOverflow else let p' ← p.multXdiffAssignTrailing (offset - i) pi.x lagrangeInterpolatePrepareLoop pts offset (i + 1) rem p'

def lagrangeInterpolatePrepareL258–266 ↗#

Poly::lagrange_interpolate_prepare (src/encoding/polynomial.rs:148–168): computes $\prod_i (x - \mathrm{pts}[i].x)$ of degree pts.length.

def lagrangeInterpolatePrepare (pts : List Pt) : Except PolyPanic Poly := do let offset := pts.length if offset + 1 > USIZE_MAX then .error .addOverflow else let p0 : Poly := { coefficients := List.replicate offset GF16.ZERO ++ [GF16.ONE] } lagrangeInterpolatePrepareLoop pts offset 0 offset p0

def lagrangeDenominatorL268–273 ↗#

def lagrangeDenominator (pix : GF16) (pts : List Pt) : GF16 := pts.foldl (fun denominator pj => if pix == pj.x then denominator else GF16.mul denominator (GF16.sub pix pj.x)) GF16.ONE

def lagrangeCompleteDivLoopL275–291 ↗#

def lagrangeCompleteDivLoop (pix scale : GF16) (len : Nat) : Nat → Nat → List GF16 → Except PolyPanic (List GF16) | _, 0, coeffs => .ok coeffs | j, rem + 1, coeffs => if j > len then .error .subOverflow else let idx := len - j if idx == 0 then .error .subOverflow else match coeffs[idx]?, coeffs[idx - 1]? with | some cIdx, some cPrev => let negativeDelta := GF16.mul cIdx pix let coeffs1 := coeffs.set idx (GF16.mul cIdx scale) let coeffs2 := coeffs1.set (idx - 1) (GF16.add cPrev negativeDelta) lagrangeCompleteDivLoop pix scale len (j + 1) rem coeffs2 | _, _ => .error .boundsCheck

def lagrangeInterpolateCompleteL293–305 ↗#

Poly::lagrange_interpolate_complete (src/encoding/polynomial.rs:202–228): divides $(x - \mathrm{pts}[i].x)$ out of self into upper coefficients [1..] and scales by $\mathrm{pts}[i].y / \prod_{p_j.x \ne \mathrm{pts}[i].x} (\mathrm{pts}[i].x - p_j.x)$.

def lagrangeInterpolateComplete (self : Poly) (pts : List Pt) (i : Nat) : Except PolyPanic Poly := do let some pi := pts[i]? | .error .boundsCheck let denominator := lagrangeDenominator pi.x pts let scale := GF16.div pi.y denominator let len := self.coefficients.length if len <= 1 then return self else let coeffs' ← lagrangeCompleteDivLoop pi.x scale len 1 (len - 1) self.coefficients return { coefficients := coeffs' }

def lagrangeAccumulateCoeffsL307–316 ↗#

def lagrangeAccumulateCoeffs : Nat → Nat → List GF16 → List GF16 → Except PolyPanic (List GF16) | _, 0, outCoeffs, _ => .ok outCoeffs | j, rem + 1, outCoeffs, workingCoeffs => if j + 1 > USIZE_MAX then .error .addOverflow else match outCoeffs[j]?, workingCoeffs[j + 1]? with | some o, some w => lagrangeAccumulateCoeffs (j + 1) rem (outCoeffs.set j (GF16.add o w)) workingCoeffs | _, _ => .error .boundsCheck

def lagrangeInterpolateLoopL318–324 ↗#

def lagrangeInterpolateLoop (template : Poly) (pts : List Pt) : Nat → Nat → List GF16 → Except PolyPanic (List GF16) | _, 0, outCoeffs => .ok outCoeffs | i, rem + 1, outCoeffs => do let working ← template.lagrangeInterpolateComplete pts i let outCoeffs' ← lagrangeAccumulateCoeffs 0 outCoeffs.length outCoeffs working.coefficients lagrangeInterpolateLoop template pts (i + 1) rem outCoeffs'

def lagrangeInterpolateL326–338 ↗#

Poly::lagrange_interpolate (src/encoding/polynomial.rs:110–141): returns the Lagrange interpolating polynomial of degree < pts.length.

def lagrangeInterpolate (pts : List Pt) : Except PolyPanic Poly := do if pts.isEmpty then return Poly.zero pts.length else let template ← Poly.lagrangeInterpolatePrepare pts let working0 ← template.lagrangeInterpolateComplete pts 0 match working0.coefficients with | [] => .error .sliceIndexFail | _ :: rest0 => let outCoeffs ← lagrangeInterpolateLoop template pts 1 (pts.length - 1) rest0 return { coefficients := outCoeffs }

def lagrangeInterpolatePtL340–347 ↗#

Poly::lagrange_interpolate_pt (src/encoding/polynomial.rs:236–242): Lagrange basis polynomial for pts[i].

def lagrangeInterpolatePt (pts : List Pt) (i : Nat) : Except PolyPanic Poly := do let result ← Poly.lagrangeInterpolatePrepare pts let result ← result.lagrangeInterpolateComplete pts i match result.coefficients with | [] => .error .sliceIndexFail | _ :: rest => return { coefficients := rest }

def computeAtPowersLoopL360–366 ↗#

def computeAtPowersLoop : Nat → Nat → List GF16 → Except PolyPanic (List GF16) | _, 0, xs => .ok xs | i, rem + 1, xs => match xs[i / 2]?, xs[(i / 2) + (i % 2)]? with | some a, some b => computeAtPowersLoop (i + 1) rem (xs ++ [GF16.mul a b]) | _, _ => .error .boundsCheck

def computeAtL368–374 ↗#

Poly::compute_at (src/encoding/polynomial.rs:261–278): evaluates self at x.

def computeAt (self : Poly) (x : GF16) : Except PolyPanic GF16 := do let len := self.coefficients.length let xs0 : List GF16 := [GF16.ONE, x] let xs ← if len <= 2 then .ok xs0 else computeAtPowersLoop 2 (len - 2) xs0 let pairs := self.coefficients.zip xs return pairs.foldl (fun out (a, b) => GF16.add out (GF16.mul a b)) GF16.ZERO

def lagrangeSumL376–380 ↗#

Poly::lagrange_sum (src/encoding/polynomial.rs:282–290): $\sum_i \mathrm{polys}[i] \cdot \mathrm{pts}[i].y$.

def lagrangeSum (pts : List Pt) (polys : List Poly) : Poly := (pts.zip polys).foldl (fun out (pt, poly) => let p := poly.multAssign pt.y out.addAssign p) (Poly.zero pts.length)
end Poly

def multL396–397 ↗#

def mult {n : Nat} (self : PolyConst n) (m : GF16) : PolyConst n := { coefficients := self.coefficients.map (fun c => GF16.constMul c m) }

def multXdiffL399–413 ↗#

PolyConst::<N>::mult_xdiff (src/encoding/polynomial.rs:428–467): multiplies self by $(x - \mathrm{difference})$ within n coefficients; panics on n == 0 (.subOverflow) or non-zero top coefficient (.explicitPanic).

def multXdiff {n : Nat} (self : PolyConst n) (difference : GF16) : Except PolyPanic (PolyConst n) := do if n == 0 then .error .subOverflow else let some top := self.coefficients[n - 1]? | .error .boundsCheck if top != GF16.ZERO then .error .explicitPanic else let xp : List GF16 := GF16.ZERO :: self.coefficients.take (n - 1) let dp : List GF16 := self.coefficients.map (fun c => GF16.constMul c difference) let out : List GF16 := (xp.zip dp).map (fun (a, b) => GF16.constSub a b) return { coefficients := out }

def lagrangeInterpolatePtLoopL415–425 ↗#

def lagrangeInterpolatePtLoop (n : Nat) (pts : List Pt) (pix : GF16) : Nat → Nat → PolyConst n → GF16 → Except PolyPanic (PolyConst n × GF16) | _, 0, p, denominator => .ok (p, denominator) | j, rem + 1, p, denominator => do let some pj := pts[j]? | .error .boundsCheck if pix == pj.x then lagrangeInterpolatePtLoop n pts pix (j + 1) rem p denominator else let p' ← p.multXdiff pj.x let denominator' := GF16.constMul denominator (GF16.constSub pix pj.x) lagrangeInterpolatePtLoop n pts pix (j + 1) rem p' denominator'

def lagrangeInterpolatePtL427–435 ↗#

PolyConst::<N>::lagrange_interpolate_pt (src/encoding/polynomial.rs:383–408).

def lagrangeInterpolatePt (n : Nat) (pts : List Pt) (i : Nat) : Except PolyPanic (PolyConst n) := do let some pi := pts[i]? | .error .boundsCheck if n == 0 then .error .boundsCheck else let p0 : PolyConst n := { coefficients := GF16.ONE :: List.replicate (n - 1) GF16.ZERO } let (p, denominator) ← lagrangeInterpolatePtLoop n pts pi.x 0 n p0 GF16.ONE return p.mult (GF16.constDiv pi.y denominator)

def checkCompletePointsL470–476 ↗#

def fromCompletePointsL478–510 ↗#

Poly::from_complete_points (src/encoding/polynomial.rs:297–330): interpolates pts when pts[i].x == i, using COMPLETE_POINTS_POLYS_{1,3,5,30,34,36} for matching lengths and Poly.lagrangeInterpolatePt otherwise.

def fromCompletePoints (pts : List Pt) : Except PolyPanic (Except Unit Poly) := do if !checkCompletePoints 0 pts then return .error () else let n := pts.length let polys : List Poly ← if n == 0 then pure [] else if n == 1 then do let cps ← COMPLETE_POINTS_POLYS_1 pure (constPolysToPolys cps) else if n == 3 then do let cps ← COMPLETE_POINTS_POLYS_3 pure (constPolysToPolys cps) else if n == 5 then do let cps ← COMPLETE_POINTS_POLYS_5 pure (constPolysToPolys cps) else if n == 30 then do let cps ← COMPLETE_POINTS_POLYS_30 pure (constPolysToPolys cps) else if n == 34 then do let cps ← COMPLETE_POINTS_POLYS_34 pure (constPolysToPolys cps) else if n == 36 then do let cps ← COMPLETE_POINTS_POLYS_36 pure (constPolysToPolys cps) else do let ones : List Pt := pts.map (fun pt => { x := pt.x, y := GF16.ONE }) (List.range n).mapM (fun i => Poly.lagrangeInterpolatePt ones i) return .ok (Poly.lagrangeSum pts polys)
